summary.value: The Sulmtaler is a heavy farm chicken from the Sulm valley and nearby valleys of Styria, south of Graz in Austria. Local birds there were fattened on maize for the table. In the late 1800s they were crossed with Cochin, Houdan and Dorking, then bred back to the old type, and by 1900 the breed stood on its own before spreading to Germany, the Netherlands and Britain. Roosters weigh about 6.6 to 8.8 pounds and hens about 5.5 to 7.7 pounds. Gold wheaten is the classic color, and both sexes carry a small crest. Hens rarely go broody and lay some 130 to 180 cream to light brown eggs a year. Birds grow fast, forage well and handle cold and wet weather. They can be flighty at first but calm down with handling, so they suit keepers who have room for them to range.
